# Implementation {#sec-implementation}

## Architecture {#sec-architecture}

::: stub
To be written in #32 from ADR 0001 and #29–#31. It will cover:

- A FastAPI service that owns data, models, pipeline, evaluation and persistence, and a React client that only renders what the service returns.
- Webcam frames streamed from the browser over a WebSocket, a one-slot latest-frame buffer, inference off the event loop.
- The service bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
:::

## Storage and privacy {#sec-storage}

::: stub
To be written in #32 from ADR 0003 and ADR 0004. It will cover:

- Enrolled photos as the source of truth, with an embedding under every recognition model made at enrollment, so switching the active model needs no re-enrollment.
- Photos, embeddings and sighting crops as BLOBs in SQLite with `secure_delete` and foreign keys on, so a purge is one cascading transaction.
- Uploads stored with orientation applied and all metadata, GPS included, stripped; sightings keep the best face crop, never the whole frame.
:::

## API {#sec-api}

::: stub
To be written in #32 from #12. It will cover:

- The REST surface under `/api`, RFC 9457 problem responses with stable codes (`no_face`, `multiple_faces`, `face_too_small`, `warnings`, `last_photo`).
- The `/api/monitor` WebSocket: binary frames in, typed JSON messages out; the runner-up and landmarks never sent live.
- The contract pipeline: the committed `openapi.json`, generated client types, and hand-written Effect schemas that fail type-checking on drift.
:::
